title: Cap. IX vocatione Sol cont.: 'precise/absolute elect cannot be commanded to believe' misreads absolute election as cutting off means
pass_a_gloss: Further, what was put in the argument, that it cannot be commanded unto the precisely or absolutely elect or reprobate that they believe, if in that sense they take those precisely and absolutely elected unto salvation so as to cut them off from the use of means, as if God had decreed to bring some unto salvation even if they reject the means of salvation, or to damn some even if they shall have believed in Christ, they thrust their own dreams upon us for our dogma.
pass_b_english: They also put it that the precisely or absolutely elect or reprobate cannot be commanded to believe. Take that in their sense of people elected to salvation so precisely that means drop out — as if God had decreed to bring some to salvation even though they reject every means of it, or to damn some even though they believe in Christ. That is not our dogma. It is their dream forced onto ours.
source_text: Porro quod in argumento positum fuit, Precise sive absolute electis aut reprobis non posse mandari ut credant, si eo sensu accipiunt precise et absolute ad salutem electos, ut praescindant ab usu mediorum, quasi Deus decrevisset aliquos ad salutem perducere etiamsi media salutis rejiciant, aut aliquos damnare, etiamsi in Christum crediderint, pro nostro dogmate sua insomnia obtrudunt.
